chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:
"There is no continuous fasting in fasting, nor silence for a day until the night."

key_terms.اللَّيْلِ: the night, marking the endpoint mentioned in the statement
key_terms.صَمْتَ: remaining silent or refraining from speech
key_terms.صِيَامٍ: fasting as an act of worship
key_terms.وِصَالَ: continuous fasting without breaking the fast between days
key_terms.يَوْمًا: a day; the duration mentioned for silence

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about continuous fasting and remaining silent all day?
ai.summary: This hadith states two prohibitions in devotional practice: continuous fasting without breaking it, and observing a vow of silence throughout the day until night. It reflects regulated worship in Islam, in which acts of devotion must conform to the prescribed sunnah (prophetic tradition).

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "There is no continuous fasting (wisal) in fasting, nor remaining silent for a day until night."
